rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
reason: Accepted research calls Phi Pop often shapeless (c29), inhabiting a living human host (c09/c25) and appearing human by day (c34). The black-dog form (c05) has no documented distinguishing anatomy or visible non-gory active power. Its other physical manifestation is host illness or internal viscera consumption (c30), which would show an ordinary sick person or require gore. Floating heads/organs belong to other ghost depictions and are not assigned here. Cannot meet the distinct-subject/sangar requirement without inventing anatomy or effects; no generation call.
